judgePersona: Senior engineer who debugs mirage agents all day with Redux DevTools + Chrome DevTools + a source-level debugger permanently open. Impatient: wants dense, fast, keyboard-first surfaces, exact diffs, and zero ceremony. Allergic to dashboards, modals, ops-inbox vibes, and anything that buries the timeline. Grounded my scores by verifying the actual plumbing: _console_trajectory returns idx+op+kind+path+mount_prefix+source+bytes+duration_ms+timestamp+effect_class+capture_state (so the data->trace reverse-link and the gap-free reconstruction cursor are EXACT and real); useEventStream reads global relay seq while _stream_agui_events bypasses _persist_and_broadcast (so the two-counter/timestamp-merge problem is real and all three are honest about it); replayAguiEvents is a true deterministic fold-from-empty; northhill_corp mounts 13 Fake*Resource(disk) backends with only / (RAM) and /tickets writeable (so overlay/time-travel is real but the writeable surface is thin, while the 12 read sources make the wrong-file/stale-read workflow the richest demo story); /database has the real tables/<t>/{schema.json,data.jsonl,stats.json} layout; catalog-proxy is 100% NotImplementedError. All reusable components (RunTracePanel/StepCard/ToolCallRow/OverlayDiff/BranchTree/TrajectoryPage/StatePage) and console endpoints exist. Scoring rewards: literal DevTools feel, exact op-level diffs, density, and honest grounding; penalizes: derived/inferred surfaces sold as exact, heavy chrome, and burying the time-travel cursor.

rankings.notes: This is the one a Redux/DevTools native will feel in their hands. The thesis is the most honest reading of the brief: workspace = store, data-plane I/O = actions, time-travel cursor = the spine, and the trace waterfall / data explorer are LENSES and DOCKS over one cursor rather than separate pages. That single-organism commitment (44px header, 380px action list, lens-tab inspector, full-width transport, collapsible data dock) is exactly the dense keyboard-first surface I want — Space to play, up/down to step, Home/End, Cmd-K, permalinks. devConsoleFeel is a 10: nobody else is this literal about being Redux DevTools, and crucially it earns it via the EXACT op-level diff (action idx == OpRecord[idx]) which I verified is real in _console_trajectory — the one diff move a wrapper competitor cannot make truthfully. leveragesMirageData is a 10: every row, fold, and diff maps to a real endpoint, and the honesty overlays (seq vs §seq gutter, inferred-order hairline, cache-derived chip, 'state (snapshot)' reserved dimmed node for dead enum names, 'pinned at stand-up' backing) are precisely calibrated to what I confirmed the plane emits. Where it loses points for MY workflow: allTracesCoverage is a 7 — 'see ALL runs' is a grouping TOGGLE (Flat <-> By run/step) on the flat list, which is elegant and dense but means scanning 6 runs for the red RUN_ERROR is a derived re-render, not a first-class run rail I can eyeball instantly; Workbench's dedicated run-lane overview beats it for the 'which trace blew up' glance. dataSourceExploration 8: the docked bidirectional bridge is excellent and the reverse-link join is exact, but demoting Data to a 36px strip undersells the richest part of THIS demo (12 read sources, only 2 writeable) — the wrong-file/stale-read story is where the demo data actually lives and the Spine keeps it docked-away by default. learnability 7: the 'no home page, the log IS the structure' purity is beautiful to me but the two-index gutter (seq/§seq) and lens-vs-page mental model is a real ramp for a teammate; the payoff is worth it but it isn't instant. implementability 7: most of it reuses shipped pieces (OverlayDiff as the hunk seed, replayAguiEvents proven, TrajectoryPage exportJson), but the unified virtualized merged-stream with future-dimming + transport playback + skip-refold + arcadia_store pagination is real net-new work, and the headline 'scrub everything in one stream' rests on the timestamp-merge until Phase-0 stamps ids.

The Chrome-DevTools-docked-over-the-page reading, and it's the most COMPLETE dev surface: five simultaneously-visible panels (waterfall, event log, data tree, state inspector, console dock) wired to one global cursor, with solo-on-double-click, drag-to-dock, tab-stacking, and layout presets. debugWorkflowFit 9 because 'one cursor lights up every panel at once' is genuinely how I debug a web app — click a write op and watch the waterfall step, the data tree path, and the state overlay all snap together. allTracesCoverage is the best of the three at 9: it has an explicit All-Traces run-lane overview screen AND a run rail in the waterfall, so the 'which of my 6 runs is red' glance is first-class, not a derived toggle — that matters to me a lot. devConsoleFeel 9: docked panels + scrubber minimap + Cmd-K is dead-on DevTools, very slightly less PURE than Spine because it hedges (keeps Compare, a separate State mode, governance chips) instead of committing to one organism. leveragesMirageData 9: same exact grounding as Spine (dense trajectory idx as the reconstruction cursor, two-stream merge with tie-markers, the VfsOp leaf under each tool call), docked one notch only because spreading the same data across five panels adds surface without adding new ground-truth leverage. Where it bleeds for me: implementability is a 5 and that's the real problem — a react-resizable multi-dock with draggable dividers, tab-groups, solo/restore, per-workspace persisted layouts, AND five live virtualized cross-highlighting panels is a large build with real perf/jank risk; the design itself names 'five live panels + cross-highlight on every cursor move' as an overload/jank risk. learnability 6: powerful but the most surface to learn at once; a new teammate faces five panels + a dock system + a breadcrumb cross-filter before they've found the timeline. As an impatient engineer I love living in it once it's built, but I don't trust it ships dense-and-fast on the first cut, and overload is a genuine threat to the 'fast' part of my requirement.

The boldest and most differentiated thesis, and the 'find-usages for data' metaphor is the single best idea in the whole set — I verified it is EXACT, not inferred-at-the-join: _console_trajectory carries mount_prefix+path so 'who read/wrote this byte' is a real client-side filter, and on THIS demo (12 read-only sources, wrong-file/stale-read is the richest failure story) the data-correctness workflow is the most valuable thing a mirage-only console can do. dataSourceExploration is a clean 10: the type-aware skins over the real ls/cat substrate, the TableCard built on the confirmed schema.json/data.jsonl/stats.json fixtures, the honest greyed metadata strip (fingerprint/revision dropped by _parse_ls_output), and the disabled query bar (catalog-proxy = 100% NotImplementedError, confirmed) are all exactly right — this is the deepest, most honest data explorer of the three. leveragesMirageData 10 for the same reasons plus the explicit 'observed below the tool args' correctness framing. BUT — and this is why it isn't my top pick despite tying high — the brief's own words are 'like the Redux DevTools console', and as a DevTools-native debugger my hand reaches for the action timeline FIRST. Sourcescope demotes the Redux centerpiece (Action Log + Time-Travel) to MODE 3 behind a data catalog home. debugWorkflowFit 8 and devConsoleFeel 8: the DataGrip-tree + DevTools-timeline cross is a real dev tool and I respect it, but data-first is a deliberate bet against my muscle memory — the design even admits 'engineers may expect a trace-first console (LangSmith muscle memory)' — and for an impatient time-travel debugger, putting the cursor a tab away is a tax I feel on every session. allTracesCoverage 7: Traces is a proper mode with a run list + rollups (good), but it's one of three modes rather than always-visible, so the all-runs glance costs a mode switch. learnability 6: the data-first inversion is the least familiar starting point; it only pays off if Touched-by is instantly discoverable, otherwise it reads as an extra hop to the traces I wanted. implementability 7: comparable to Spine, helped by reusing StatePage/VFSExplorer/RunTracePanel wholesale, with the same merged-stream + state-fold net-new work. Net: the strongest IDEAS, slightly wrong DEFAULT for the stated 'Redux DevTools' feel.

bestIdeasToGraft: Sourcescope's 'find-usages for data' / 'who touched this byte?' framing — the single best idea in the set. It is the moat made literal (IDE find-usages, but the symbol index is the mount catalog and the call sites are traces/steps), and I verified the join is EXACT off _console_trajectory's mount_prefix+path, not inferred. Whatever ships MUST adopt this as the headline data->trace gesture, not a buried feature.

Sourcescope's read/write sparkline + touch-count badge per path ('written once, read 30x') and the explicit wrong-file / stale-revision investigation FLOW (suspect path -> Touched-by shows a sibling/older path was read -> jump to that op -> scrub state to confirm what had/hadn't been read yet). On this demo's 12 read-only sources, this is the most valuable debugging story the console can tell — bake the named workflow in, not just the primitives.

Sourcescope's type-aware data skins over the SAME ls/cat substrate: the TableCard (Schema/Rows/Stats from the real schema.json/data.jsonl/stats.json fixtures) and per-source 'browsed as: file tree / table' subtitle. It adds honest value to disk-doubled exotic sources without faking a native client or a query engine.

Spine's EXACT per-action git-hunk diff for VfsOps grounded in action idx == OpRecord[idx], reusing OverlayDiff as the hunk renderer. This is the truthful diff no wrapper competitor can make and must be the centerpiece of the inspector's Diff lens.

Spine's lens-over-one-cursor model: Flat <-> By-run/step is a GROUPING TOGGLE on the same action list, and Diff/State/Action/Trace/Data are TABS over the same selected action — not separate routes. This is the densest, most DevTools-faithful way to avoid page-switching.

Spine's transport bar (mini-map scrubber + play/pause/step/jump + speed) with future-dimming on both rows and the mini-map, plus keyboard-first operation (Space play, up/down step, Home/End, Cmd-K). This is the literal Redux time-travel feel the brief asks for.

Workbench's first-class All-Traces run-lane overview (newest-first run lanes with status dots + rollups) — the fastest 'which of my N runs is red' glance, which both Spine and Sourcescope make a derived toggle/mode. Graft this as a dedicated, always-cheap run rail rather than only a grouping view.

Workbench's 'one cursor lights up every panel at once' synchronized selection and its honest 'hypothetical: action N skipped' what-if banner with one-click revert for skip-action (scoped to the reconstructable overlay/reads/run layers).

The honesty vocabulary shared across all three, which I confirmed against the plane and which is non-negotiable: seq vs §seq gutter + 'inferred order' tie-marker for the timestamp-merge; 'served from cache (derived)' ghost rows (cache emits no OpRecord); 'backing pinned at stand-up' on full-FS time travel; greyed 'not yet emitted' rails for STATE_DELTA/lineage/policy; disabled query bar for catalog-proxy NotImplementedError; greyed fingerprint/revision where _parse_ls_output drops them; 'preview only / truncated / binary' on cat output; and the 'inferred' dot on every op->step attribution until tool_call_id is stamped.

Permalink-everything + Export/Import session bundle (generalize TrajectoryPage.exportJson + the agui trace into a replayable .mirage-session.json) — present in all three; keep it as the 'hand the repro to a teammate' affordance.
synthesisAdvice:
Ship Spine as the structural skeleton — it is the only design that commits to the literal Redux DevTools organism the brief demands (workspace = store, data-plane I/O = actions, one time-travel cursor as the spine, trace waterfall and data explorer as LENSES/DOCKS not pages). Do not water this down into Workbench's five-panel dock: that is more product but loses the sharp single-spine feel and carries real first-cut perf/jank and build-cost risk (its own listed overload risk). The skeleton: 44px header (workspace switcher + Cmd-K + quiet mode glyph + persisted/in-memory pill), a virtualized merged action list on the left with Flat<->By-run/step grouping, a lens-tab inspector (Diff / State Tree / Action / Trace / Data) over the single selected action, and a full-width transport bar with future-dimming. State reconstruction folds the gap-free trajectory idx; the VfsOp Diff is the exact OpRecord hunk via OverlayDiff.

Then graft Sourcescope's data thesis as the equal SECOND pillar — because on THIS demo (12 read-only sources, only RAM+/tickets writeable) the wrong-file/stale-read, data-correctness workflow is the single most valuable thing a mirage-only console can do, and the reverse-link join is provably EXACT. Concretely: (1) promote the Data dock from a 36px strip to a real, instantly-openable pillar (keyboard 1/2/3-style or Cmd-\) with Sourcescope's full mount catalog + type-aware TableCard skin + Touched-by panel + read/write sparkline; (2) make 'find-usages for data' (click a path's touch-count -> Touched-by list -> click an op -> global cursor jumps + Diff lens highlights) a headline gesture, and keep the inverse automatic (cursor on a VfsOp auto-reveals+rings the path); (3) bake in the named wrong-file/stale-revision FLOW as a first-class story, not just primitives. Keep the cursor and the path as the two shared URL-addressable selections so every cross-pillar jump is a permalink — this is the bridge that makes Spine's timeline and Sourcescope's catalog one tool instead of two tabs.

From Workbench, take exactly ONE thing: a first-class, always-cheap All-Traces run-lane overview (run lanes with status dots + rollups, newest-first) so 'which of my runs is red' is an instant glance, not a derived grouping re-render. Wire selecting a lane to scope the spine. Leave Workbench's dock system, Compare, and separate State mode out of v1 (Compare and a State browser can be later lenses; the StatePage code is reusable when you get there).

Governance stays demoted everywhere per the reframe: effect-class dot + reversibility tooltip as quiet per-write decorations, a non-alarming mode glyph, promote reachable only from Cmd-K — never a modal front door. 

Non-negotiable engineering order: (a) virtualize the action list and paginate off arcadia_store from day one — a console watching ALL workspace events cannot ride the 2000-event RAM ring or it goes empty after restart, so surface the persisted-vs-in-memory pill prominently; (b) carry the entire shared honesty vocabulary (two-index gutter + inferred-order tie-marker, cache-derived ghost rows, pinned-at-stand-up backing, greyed not-yet-emitted rails, disabled query bar, greyed dropped fingerprint/revision, inferred op->step dot) — these are calibrated to exactly what I confirmed the plane emits and softening any of them turns truth into a lie; (c) prioritize the Phase-0 plumbing (stamp tool_call_id/run_id/step_id + restore source/duration_ms/fingerprint/revision on op emission, consume ExecutionNode.records) because it simultaneously upgrades the merged-stream ordering from timestamp-approximate to exact AND upgrades every op->step attribution from inferred to joined — it is the highest-leverage backend fix for the whole synthesis.

judgePersona: A UX designer who has shipped beloved keyboard-first developer tools (the kind of person who knows Redux DevTools, Chrome DevTools, and a real source-level debugger by muscle memory) and who has read the actual Mirage codebase — so I score by dev-console feel and debugging flow, but I dock points hard for anything that the real endpoints (gap-free trajectory idx, two-counter seq, ls/cat-only VFS, NotImplementedError catalog-proxy) cannot actually back.

rankings.notes: The most disciplined dev-console feel of the three and the only one that takes 'Redux DevTools, literally' at its word: one persistent two-pane organism (Action List + State Inspector) with a transport pinned across the bottom, lenses (Diff/State/Action/Trace/Data) instead of pages, Cmd-K, future-dimming, import/export, permalinks. This is exactly the keyboard-first, information-dense, cross-linked-panel feel the reframe demands — it deletes the routed SUB_NAV page-switcher (which I confirmed is literally how ConsoleLayout works today) and replaces it with a single cursor. devConsoleFeel is a clean 10. The Diff lens is the sharpest single move in any design: I verified _console_overlay's change key is exactly idx:op:path and the trajectory idx is gap-free enumerate(records), so 'action N == OpRecord[N]' makes the per-write hunk EXACT, not a guess — no wrapper competitor can do this. debugWorkflowFit is high but not max: a single 380px rail showing ALL actions flat is superb for op-level debugging but cramped for eyeballing reasoning+data+state SIMULTANEOUSLY (Workbench's docked panels win there). The two real weaknesses are structural, not cosmetic: (1) allTracesCoverage — 'all traces' is a *grouping toggle* (Flat <-> By run/step) on the same rail, which is elegant but means there is no dedicated run-overview surface to scan 6 runs and spot the red one at a glance; collapsing 5000 flat actions into a run tree in a 380px rail is dense to the point of strain. (2) dataSourceExploration — the Data Dock is deliberately a collapsed 36px strip, so the rich northhill_corp catalog (/database,/s3,/datadog,/slack,/pagerduty,/github — I confirmed the incident_forensics task spans 6 mounts) is demoted to a side panel; the bidirectional bridge is excellent but you browse data in a cramped dock. implementability is genuinely good: it reuses TrajectoryPage (filter row + exportJson + getConsoleFile already exist), replayAguiEvents (real fold-from-empty), OverlayDiff, and the console endpoints — but the time-travel cursor / stateAt(N) does NOT exist today (I grepped: only CSS cursor:pointer), and the dock-free single-organism shell is a from-scratch reshell, so it is not free. Honesty is the best of the three: seq vs §seq in the gutter, 'inferred order' hairline, reserved dimmed STATE_SNAPSHOT node, 'pinned at stand-up' backing, greyed query.json — every caveat I checked maps to real code.

The best DEBUGGING tool of the three and the strongest at the reframe's literal ask ('see ALL the traces AND offer data-source exploration') because five simultaneously-visible docked panels — waterfall, event log, data tree, state inspector, console — driven by one global cursor is exactly how you live in Chrome DevTools all day. debugWorkflowFit is the highest here: clicking a write op lights the owning step in the waterfall, flashes the path in the data tree, and re-folds state with a single-op diff — all on screen at once. That synchronized-selection-across-panels move is the truest 'real dev console' behavior and is why allTracesCoverage is a 9: it is the ONLY design with a dedicated All-Traces screen (run-rail of collapsible lanes with status dots + rollups, newest-first, virtualized) AND a single-trace waterfall AND the flat log — three honest ways to see traces, where Spine has one rail-toggle and Sourcescope buries the log at mode 3. devConsoleFeel is high (8) but a notch below Spine: a draggable react-resizable dock with tab-groups, solo-on-double-click, and layout presets feels like VS Code/DevTools, but five live panels is also where it stops feeling like the surgical single-purpose Redux organism and starts risking the 'busy IDE' middle ground — and the reframe explicitly invoked Redux DevTools first. The two real costs: (1) implementability is the lowest — a persistent resizable multi-panel dock with per-workspace layout persistence, five panels each reading paginated/virtualized endpoints, plus the same net-new time-travel cursor everyone needs, is materially more infra than Spine's two-pane shell or Sourcescope's router reuse; the design even admits the firehose is GLOBAL and only console_* carry workspace_id, so workspace-scoping ALL five panels is real plumbing. (2) learnability — five docked panels + cross-filter bus is the steepest first-run cliff; mitigated by presets and collapsible docks, but a new dev faces the most surface at once. leveragesMirageData ties Spine: same OpRecord leaf, same exact single-op diff, same real two-stream merge, reuses RunTracePanel/StepCard/ToolCallRow and VFSExplorer vocabulary. Honesty is strong and identical in kind (≈ tie-markers, ghost cache rows, greyed not-yet-emitted rails, pinned-backing label).

rankings.approach: Sourcescope — the Bidirectional Data ⇄ Trace Explorer Console
rankings.notes: The sharpest THESIS and the most uniquely-Mirage of the three: 'find-usages for data' — start at a suspect path, reverse-link to every step that read/wrote it, jump to the offending op, scrub state — is the single best articulation of the moat the reframe names ('because mirage IS the data plane, bridge data<->trace, who touched this byte?'). dataSourceExploration is a clear 10: it is the only design that makes the connected sources the FRONT DOOR, with a real mount catalog (effect-class chips from _console_mounts_detail), a type-aware table skin over the genuine schema.json/data.jsonl/stats.json fixture layout I confirmed in fake_postgres.py, and a read-vs-write sparkline per path — it extracts the most from the rich northhill_corp catalog. leveragesMirageData is also a 10: the wrong-file/stale-revision investigation flow is the most concrete payoff of observing ground truth below the tool args, and the find-usages join is exact (I verified _console_trajectory carries mount_prefix+path). debugWorkflowFit is high (8) for the ONE workflow it optimizes (data-correctness debugging) — arguably the highest-value real-world agent bug — but a hair below Workbench/Spine as a GENERAL debugger because reasoning/latency live one mode away in TRACES. The reasons it is not the dev-console winner: (1) devConsoleFeel is the lowest (7) — it is the ONLY design that keeps the routed sibling-route page-switcher (three modes 1/2/3 under React-Router, closest to today's ConsoleLayout, which cuts both ways), and it DEMOTES the Redux time-travel centerpiece the reframe calls 'the centerpiece' to mode #3; a Redux-DevTools-grade console whose Redux surface is the third tab reads more like 'DataGrip + a timeline tab' than the single time-travel organism. (2) learnability — the design itself flags the biggest bet: data-first is a wager against trace-first muscle memory (LangSmith habit); if Touched-by isn't instantly discoverable the inversion reads as an extra hop. (3) the INFERRED-attribution dependency bites hardest HERE: I read correlateEventsToSteps and it assigns the LAST timestamp-matching step, so overlapping/zero-duration steps mis-bucket — and Sourcescope's headline 'this path was read by run-7/step-2' leans entirely on that until tool_call_id is stamped. implementability is solid (reuses StatePage, VFSExplorer, RunTracePanel, exportJson, and the smallest router departure) but carries the same net-new time-travel fold and the same scale/scoping work. I rank it #1 by a nose because its thesis is the most defensible and least copyable, and dataSourceExploration is half the reframe's explicit ask — but it is the design that least FEELS like the Redux dev console the user asked for, so its lead is real but narrow.

topPick: Sourcescope — narrowly, on thesis strength and uniqueness (best dataSourceExploration + leveragesMirageData, which together are half the reframe's explicit ask and the part no competitor can copy). But it is a genuine three-way near-tie (55 / 53 / 53), and the honest reading is: Sourcescope has the strongest SOUL, Spine has the strongest FEEL, Workbench has the strongest WORKFLOW. The synthesis should be built on Spine's single-organism shell, given Sourcescope's data-bridge as the headline pillar, and granted Workbench's dedicated All-Traces overview — see synthesisAdvice.
bestIdeasToGraft: Spine's single-organism shell with LENSES instead of pages (Diff / State Tree / Action / Trace / Data tabs over ONE selected action and ONE cursor) — this is the move that makes it feel like Redux DevTools rather than a routed app, and it directly deletes today's SUB_NAV page-switcher (Workspaces/run/trajectory/state/promote routes I confirmed in ConsoleLayout). The whole synthesis should inherit this shell.

Spine's EXACT per-action Diff lens for VfsOps as a git-style hunk — grounded in the verified fact that trajectory idx is gap-free and the overlay change key is idx:op:path, so action N IS OpRecord[N]. This is the single most differentiated, most-honest debugging move in any of the three; it must survive into the final design verbatim.

Sourcescope's 'find-usages for data' bidirectional bridge (data->trace) with the 'N traces' touch-count gutter on every path/table/row and the Touched-by inspector grouped by run|op — this is the clearest expression of the moat the reframe explicitly names and the sharpest real-world workflow (wrong-file / stale-revision). All three have a bridge; Sourcescope's IDE 'find-usages' framing is the most memorable and teachable version.

Sourcescope's type-aware TABLE skin (Schema / Rows / Stats sub-tabs over the real schema.json/data.jsonl/stats.json fixture layout) plus the read-vs-write sparkline per path — the most that can honestly be extracted from the disk-double backends, and it makes the data pillar feel like a real data client rather than a file dump.

Workbench's dedicated All-Traces overview (run-rail of collapsible lanes: started_at, status dot, steps/tools/bytes rollup, mini latency bar, newest-first, virtualized) — the one thing Spine genuinely lacks. 'See all traces in a workspace' is in the reframe's headline; a flat-list grouping toggle is not enough to scan many runs and spot the failing one.

Workbench's one-cursor-drives-all-panels synchronized selection and the bottom scrubber/minimap with a draggable playhead (density sparkline over wall-time, future segment dimmed) — the most tactile expression of time-travel and the part that most feels like a debugger's stack-frame scrubber.

The honesty chrome shared across all three but best-itemized in Spine/Sourcescope: seq vs §seq in the row gutter + 'inferred order' hairline on same-ms ties, the reserved dimmed STATE_SNAPSHOT/STATE_DELTA node, the 'served from cache (derived)' ghost chip, 'preview only / truncated / binary' on cat output, greyed fingerprint/revision with the '_parse_ls_output drops these' explanation, 'pinned at stand-up' on backing, and the greyed-but-present 'query.json — NotImplementedError' affordance. I verified every one of these maps to real code; keep them all, they are the trust layer.

Spine + Sourcescope's permalink + Export/Import (generalize the existing TrajectoryPage.exportJson to merged log + agui trace; import re-hydrates via replayAguiEvents into a read-only scrub) — turns a debugging session into a shareable, replayable artifact, which is exactly what a dev tool you live in needs.

Cmd-K go-to-anything routing into a shared (path, cursor-idx) URL state — present in all three but worth stating as a hard requirement: keyboard-first, every view permalinkable. Sourcescope's grouped Sources/Runs/Actions palette is the best-specified version.
synthesisAdvice: Build ONE console = Spine's shell + Sourcescope's soul + Workbench's overview. Concretely: (1) ADOPT SPINE'S SINGLE-ORGANISM SHELL as the chassis — a persistent two/three-region layout with a global cursor and a lens strip, NOT routed pages; this is what earns the 'Redux DevTools / real dev console' feel the user asked for and it deletes the current SUB_NAV router. (2) But REJECT Spine's demotion of data to a 36px strip — instead promote Sourcescope's data catalog to a first-class, always-available left panel (not a dock you have to open), because dataSourceExploration is half the reframe's explicit ask and the northhill_corp catalog (6 mounts in incident_forensics) is rich enough to carry it. Resolve the Spine-vs-Sourcescope tension by making the layout a PRESET toggle, not an argument: ship 'Time-Travel focus' (Spine's action-list + state-inspector dominant) and 'Data focus' (Sourcescope's catalog + Touched-by dominant) as two arrangements of the SAME panels and SAME cursor — borrow Workbench's layout-presets idea so you don't have to pick a single front door. (3) The find-usages bridge is the spine of the whole thing in BOTH directions and must be bidirectional and always-on: path -> Touched-by -> jump cursor (Sourcescope), and cursor-on-VfsOp -> auto-reveal+ring path in catalog (Spine). (4) ADD Workbench's dedicated All-Traces run-rail as one lens/view — do NOT rely on a flat-list grouping toggle alone; 'see ALL traces' needs a scannable run overview with status dots. (5) Keep ONE cursor across everything (Workbench's synchronized selection) with the bottom scrubber/minimap; the per-action Diff (Spine, exact for VfsOps) is the killer lens — it is the load-bearing differentiator and must be exact, not approximate. (6) NON-NEGOTIABLE engineering ordering: the entire synthesis leans on op->step attribution, and I confirmed correlateEventsToSteps is timestamp-window inference that assigns the LAST matching step (mis-buckets overlapping/zero-duration steps). Do the reframe's Phase-0 fix FIRST (stamp tool_call_id/step_id/run_id + the dropped source/duration_ms/fingerprint/revision on every VfsOp at emission, server.py ~L1403; consume ExecutionNode.records instead of length-diffing ws.ops.records). Until then, label every bridged/grouped row 'inferred' — Sourcescope's whole data->step precision and the By-run/step grouping both rest on this. (7) Second non-negotiable: the time-travel cursor / stateAt(N) does NOT exist today (verified — only CSS cursor refs), so the one net-new core engine all three need is a deterministic client-side fold of trajectory[0..idx] over the real console endpoints (_console_overlay change-key idx:op:path, _console_trajectory, _console_effects) plus replayAguiEvents sliced to the cursor timestamp; build this once, share it across every panel. (8) Standardize on arcadia_store-backed paginated/virtualized reads from day one — do NOT ship on the 2000-event RAM ring (verified MAX_EVENTS=2000 slice in useEventStream); a console watching ALL workspace events will truncate or go empty after restart otherwise, and note runs/steps/tool_calls/vfs_ops are currently WRITE-ONLY so historical post-restart views need new read queries. (9) Map workspace->session and client-side-filter, since useEventStream('/events') is global and only console_* carry workspace_id. (10) Keep the honesty chrome from all three (it is the trust layer and every caveat maps to real code) and keep governance demoted to quiet per-write effect-class dots with promote reachable only from Cmd-K — no LIVE red chrome, no pending-effects counter, per the reframe.

judgePersona: Pragmatic eng lead who has now read the actual server.py, the reducer, the console endpoints, and the fixtures — and who scores designs by what survives contact with the real plumbing (gap-free trajectory idx = solid; two-counter timestamp merge = lossy; ls/cat = name/type/size only; every exotic backend = DiskResource; catalog-proxy/query.json/STATE_DELTA = NotImplementedError or dead enum). I reward designs that put their dominant feel on the SOLID substrate and demote the lossy parts to honest decorations, and I penalize designs that hang their headline on inferred ordering or fabricated source widgets.

rankings.notes: The most honest design about the actual data, and the one that best understands WHERE the solid substrate is. It is the ONLY design that surfaces the 20-op relay cap (server.py L1006 `new_records[-20:]` vs the uncapped AG-UI CUSTOM path L1403) and resolves it correctly by preferring the trajectory/agui source for VfsOps — verified real. It alone makes the gap-free op `idx` (== ws.ops.records position, confirmed in _console_trajectory L2318) the EXPLICIT reconstruction cursor while showing seq/§seq separately in the gutter with an 'inferred order' hairline — this is the single most technically correct stance on the two-counter problem of the three. devConsoleFeel is a 10: it is literally Redux DevTools (Log/Diff/State/Action lenses over ONE action list + ONE cursor), the most authentic dev-tool feel. allTracesCoverage is strong because Flat↔By-run/step is a GROUPING LENS over the same flat stream, not a separate page — you genuinely see ALL actions and collapse to the waterfall in place. leveragesMirageData is a 10: the VfsOp diff IS OpRecord[idx] (exact, the moat move no wrapper can copy), overlay/reads/mounts fold from real endpoints, cache hits derived not faked, backing labeled pinned-at-stand-up, STATE_SNAPSHOT shown as a reserved dimmed stub (correct — it's dead enum-only, verified types/agui.ts L17-18). Costs: learnability 6 — deleting the page-switcher for a lens/dock model is powerful but unfamiliar; a LangSmith-muscle-memory dev needs orientation, and the dual seq/§seq gutter, while honest, is cognitive load. dataSourceExploration 7 — the dock is correct and bidirectional but demoted to a 36px strip by default, so the 'connected data-source exploration' pillar the reframe explicitly names is the quietest part of the loudest design. implementability 7 — the spine itself reuses exportJson/replayAguiEvents/OverlayDiff (all verified present) and the endpoints exist, but the always-mounted three-region grid + virtualized merged stream + per-lens inspector + future-dimming + skip-refold is a large net-new shell, and it still needs arcadia_store pagination to not die on the 2000-event ring.

The most COMPLETE realization of 'a tool you live in all day' — five simultaneously-visible docked panels (waterfall + event log + data tree + state + console) wired to one global cursor, Chrome-DevTools docked over the workspace. debugWorkflowFit 9: one-cursor-drives-all-panels is the strongest cross-correlation story (click an op → waterfall scrolls to owning step, data tree flashes the path, state re-folds, Diff tab shows the single op) and it's grounded — it correctly prefers the dense trajectory idx for reconstruction while merging firehose seq ⊕ agui timestamp with ≈ tie-markers (the honest stance). allTracesCoverage 9: dedicated All-Traces run-rail screen + RUN-filtered event log covers scan-all-runs well. dataSourceExploration 8 — best-developed of the three data panels short of Sourcescope: touch-count badges, Touches reverse-link, SchemaGrid for the verified tables/<t> fixture layout, honest greyed metadata. leveragesMirageData 9, on par with Spine on the exact-diff and honest-reserved-rails. Where it loses to Spine: devConsoleFeel 9 not 10 — five draggable/resizable/dockable/soloable panels is more VS-Code-layout-manager than the pure Redux spine, and the Redux time-travel centerpiece is one panel among five rather than THE organism. learnability 5 — this is the heaviest cognitive load of the three by a wide margin: five live panels + breadcrumb scope + Compare + layout presets is a lot of surface for a new dev, and the reframe's 'dense, fast' can tip into overwhelming. implementability 5 — the LOWEST of the three and the real knock: a react-resizable dock with draggable dividers, tabbed panel-groups, solo-on-double-click, persisted-per-workspace layouts, AND five live cross-filtered virtualized panels is a serious front-end build well beyond reusing exportJson/RunTracePanel/VFSExplorer; cross-highlight-on-every-cursor-move across five panels also has real perf risk the design itself flags. Strong design, but it bites off the most for the same backend gaps everyone shares.

The sharpest THESIS and the best single-workflow design: 'find-usages for data' is a genuinely novel inversion that maps perfectly onto the reframe's named moat ('who touched this byte?') and onto the verified join key (OpRecord mount_prefix+path in _console_trajectory). dataSourceExploration 10 — uncontested best: it's the only design that makes the data catalog the HOME, fully specs the type-aware skins (file-tree vs the real tables/<t> Schema/Rows/Stats card), and bakes 'touched by N traces' badges + read/write sparkline + the wrong-file/stale-revision investigation flow as the centerpiece. This is exactly the 'connected data-source exploration' pillar the reframe demands, taken furthest. leveragesMirageData 9 — same exact-diff and honest-reserved discipline as the others, plus it most explicitly ties the data→trace bridge to observe.context.record() ground truth. learnability 7 — paradoxically clean because the find-usages metaphor is one strong idea, BUT the design itself names the real risk: data-first IA bets against LangSmith muscle memory; devs reflexively want traces first, so Sources-as-home can read as 'an extra hop to the traces I wanted.' Where it loses: devConsoleFeel 7 — three sibling routed MODES (Sources/Traces/Action Log) under a workspace layout is more 'database client + DevTools tabs' than a single live Redux organism; the time-travel centerpiece is mode #3, not the spine, so the Redux-DevTools feel the reframe asks for is present but not dominant. allTracesCoverage 7 — Traces mode covers it via a run list + waterfall, fine but conventional and second-fiddle to the data home. debugWorkflowFit 8 — superb for the data-correctness workflow it's built around, but a dev whose bug is 'why did this run loop / error' starts in mode #2 and the data-first front door is friction for that case. implementability 6 — extends the existing /console React-Router tree (lower-risk than a net-new dock) and reuses StatePage/RunTracePanel/VFSExplorer/exportJson, but the Schema/Rows/Stats TableCard, the derived per-mount touched-by rollups, the sparkline, and the same state-fold engine are real net-new work, and it carries the same two-counter/scale debts.

bestIdeasToGraft: Spine's gap-free op `idx` as the EXPLICIT, primary state-reconstruction cursor (verified: _console_trajectory L2318 yields idx == ws.ops.records position) while showing relay seq / §agui-seq separately in the row gutter with an 'inferred order' hairline on same-ms collisions — this is the single most technically correct answer to the two-counter problem and ALL three designs should adopt it verbatim.

Spine's surfacing of the 20-op relay cap (server.py L1006 `new_records[-20:]`) vs the uncapped AG-UI CUSTOM(vfs_op) path, and the rule to PREFER the trajectory/agui source for VfsOp rows — the only design that caught this real discrepancy; it must be in the final.

Spine's Flat↔By-run/step GROUPING LENS over one action list (the trace waterfall as a lens, not a page) — the cleanest way to deliver 'see ALL traces' AND 'drill one trace' from a single cursor; superior to Workbench's separate All-Traces screen and Sourcescope's separate Traces mode.

Sourcescope's 'find-usages for data' / 'who touched this byte?' as the headline bidirectional bridge, with the per-path/per-mount 'touched by N traces' badge and the read/write sparkline — this is the reframe's named moat and the most differentiated workflow; it should be the data panel's reason to exist.

Sourcescope's type-aware data skins over the SAME ls/cat substrate — specifically the /database TableCard (Schema sub-tab from schema.json, Rows from data.jsonl, Stats from stats.json), validated against the real fake_postgres tables/<t> fixture layout — the most honest, highest-value way to make disk-fakes useful without faking a query engine.

Workbench's 'one cursor drives every panel at once' synchronization contract (click anything → owning step highlights, touched path flashes, state re-folds, single-op diff) — the precise cross-correlation behavior the final console needs, regardless of how many panels are visible.

The universally-shared honesty vocabulary (exact-where-VfsOp diff = OpRecord[idx]; 'served from cache' DERIVED chips, never phantom actions; backing 'pinned at stand-up'; INFERRED op→step until tool_call_id is stamped at emission per the Phase-0 fix; greyed 'not yet emitted' rails for STATE_DELTA/lineage/policy/query.json — all verified as real gaps) — adopt this discipline wholesale.

Permalink-everything (workspace + cursor idx + lens/path/selection in the URL) plus Export/Import built on the verified TrajectoryPage.exportJson + the agui_events trace — present in all three; keep it as a first-class dev-tool affordance.
synthesisAdvice: Ship Spine's SHELL with Sourcescope's DATA SOUL — they are complementary, not competing, and the synthesis is concrete. Make Spine the skeleton: one always-mounted two-pane organism (unified Action List left + State Inspector right) driven by ONE time-travel cursor keyed on the gap-free trajectory idx, with the Flat↔By-run/step grouping lens delivering both all-traces and single-trace from that one list, and lenses (Diff/State/Action/Trace) over the one selected action. This wins devConsoleFeel and is the most data-honest spine. Then fix Spine's one real weakness — it demotes the reframe's explicitly-named data-exploration pillar to a 36px strip — by promoting the Data Sources panel from a quiet dock to a FIRST-CLASS, full-height surface built to Sourcescope's spec: the mount catalog with effect-class chips and 'touched by N traces' badges as the home affordance, the type-aware TableCard/file-tree skins over ls/cat, and the 'find-usages for data' reverse-link as the headline bidirectional bridge. Borrow Workbench's exact one-cursor-drives-all synchronization contract to wire the data panel and the spine together (click a path's touch → cursor jumps; park cursor on a VfsOp → path auto-reveals), but DECLINE Workbench's five-draggable-panels dock manager — it has the worst implementability (5) and learnability (5) and adds layout-engine complexity for no proportional debug payoff; a fixed, resizable, collapsible 2-to-3-region layout (spine + promotable data panel) gets 90% of the value at a third of the build. Resolve the data-first-vs-trace-first IA tension (Sourcescope's biggest risk vs LangSmith habit) by NOT routing modes: default to the spine (trace/action centric, familiar) but make the data catalog one keystroke / one dock-expand away and bidirectionally linked, so the data inversion is always reachable without forcing it as the front door. Sequence the build to ride only the SOLID substrate first: Phase 1 = spine + Diff lens on VfsOps (exact, the moat, ships on existing endpoints + exportJson/replayAguiEvents/OverlayDiff, all verified present); Phase 2 = grouping lens + Data panel with touched-by bridge; Phase 3 (gated on the Phase-0 emission fix to stamp tool_call_id/run_id + the dropped source/duration_ms/fingerprint/revision onto VfsOps at server.py L1403, and on arcadia_store pagination to escape the 2000-event ring) = remove the INFERRED labels and the timestamp-merge hairline. Until Phase-0 lands, keep every INFERRED/derived/pinned/not-yet-emitted label exactly as all three designs specify — that honesty is the product's credibility and is non-negotiable given the verified gaps (two-counter merge, 20-op cap, ls/cat fidelity ceiling, all-NotImplementedError catalog-proxy/query.json, dead STATE_DELTA enum).
